si_4_title.answer: Normative Modeling of Brain Morphometry in Clinical High Risk for Psychosis

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Multivariable Fractional Polynomial Regression (MFPR) was identified as the optimal algorithm through a benchmarking process within the CentileBrain framework.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Through this pipeline, we identified multivariable fractional polynomial regression as the optimal algorithm
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Haas2024.pdf.md: Methods / Normative Modeling of Brain Morphometry

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled regional measures of cortical thickness (CT) (n=68), surface area (SA) (n=68), and subcortical volume (SV) (n=14) parcellated using FreeSurfer.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: regional measures of CT (n = 68), surface area (SA) (n = 68), and subcortical volume (SV) (n = 14).

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative models were sex-specific and age-dependent (3-90 years). They included site harmonization (ComBat-GAM) and global neuroimaging measures as covariates (ICV for SV models, mean CT for CT models, and mean SA for SA models).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: Sex-specific normative models... aged 3-90 years... optimal covariate combination involved site harmonization (ComBat-GAM) and the inclusion of intracranial volume, mean CT, and mean SA in the models of the regional measures of SV, CT, and SA, respectively.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Haas2024.pdf.md: Methods / Normative Modeling of Brain Morphometry
